units.source_text: 薰大将走到东面的走廊边，看见开着的门口有许多侍女正在低声谈话。

en.t: General Kaoru walked to the eastern corridor and saw many ladies-in-waiting speaking quietly near the open doorway.

units.source_text: 他就对她们说：“你们应该知道我是最可亲近的人。

en.t: He said to them, "You should know that I am the easiest person to approach.

units.source_text: 女人也没有像我这样可以信托。

en.t: Even among women, there is no one you can trust as much as me.

units.source_text: 我虽然是男人，却也能把女人须知之事教给你们。

en.t: Although I am a man, I can still teach you what women need to know.

units.source_text: 你们会渐渐了解我的心情的，所以我很高兴。”

en.t: You will gradually come to understand my feelings, and that makes me very glad."

units.source_text: 众侍女都默默不能作答。

en.t: All the ladies-in-waiting remained silent and could not answer.

units.source_text: 就中有一个名叫弁姐的，是一个熟悉世故而年事较长的侍女，答道：

en.t: Among them was an older lady-in-waiting called Elder Sister Ben, experienced in the ways of the world, who replied:

units.source_text: “没有密切关系的人，总是不好意思亲近的。

en.t: "When one has no close connection with someone, it is always hard to feel at ease approaching them.

units.source_text: 不过世间的事往往相反。

en.t: But things in this world often turn out the opposite way.

units.source_text: 就像我，并非对你有密切关系而可以任意不拘地相见的人。

en.t: Take me, for example: I am not someone so closely connected to you that I may meet you freely and without restraint.

units.source_text: 然而我们这种厚着面皮当侍女的人，装作怕羞而不理睬你，不是可笑的么？”

en.t: Yet for people like us, shameless enough to serve as ladies-in-waiting, would it not be ridiculous to pretend to be shy and ignore you?"

units.source_text: 薰大将说：“你断言对我不必怕羞，我倒又觉得遗憾了。”

en.t: General Kaoru said, "When you declare that there is no need to be shy with me, I find myself rather disappointed."

units.source_text: 他向里面望望，但见脱下的唐装堆在一旁，大约正在任情不拘地弄笔。

en.t: He looked inside and saw discarded Chinese-style robes piled to one side; she had apparently been amusing herself freely with a brush.

units.source_text: 砚台盖里盛着些琐碎的小花枝，看来是她玩耍的。

en.t: The lid of the inkstone case held small, delicate flower sprigs, which seemed to be things she had been playing with.

units.source_text: 有几个侍女躲进了帷屏后面；另有几个背转了身子，向开着的门口眺望。

en.t: Several ladies-in-waiting had hidden behind the curtain screens; others had turned their backs and were gazing toward the open doorway.
Their hair was all very beautiful.

units.source_text: 薰大将便把那里的笔砚移过来，题一首诗：

en.t: General Kaoru then drew the brush and inkstone there toward him and wrote a poem:
